title: Notes on A Part-time Society
transcript:
Speaker 1: Society Representative: Hello. This is the Leighton Society. How can I help?
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Oh, hello. I’m just phoning you because I’m interested in becoming a member of your society, and I was wondering if you could give me some more information.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: Of course. What would you like to know?
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Well, first of all, I’d like to know where you hold the club meetings, as I’m not very mobile anymore, and I’m looking for somewhere that’s within walking distance of my house. Are you still down at the old boathouse?
Speaker 1: Society Representative: No. We moved away from there a while ago. Meetings are now held at the club house.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Oh, brilliant. That’s only five minutes from me. Do you require members to have any skills or experience?
Speaker 1: Society Representative: No. There is no experience required. We have plenty of female singers and actresses, but we don’t have many men who can play the male roles. We are looking to resolve this and are especially interested in recruiting male actors and singers.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: I’ve never sung professionally, but I’m very keen on it. And I’ve been told that I’m talented, so I think this would be a good fit. Do you organize coaches to transport members to practice at the theater?
Speaker 1: Society Representative: Unfortunately, the club does not have sufficient funds to organize transportation, though this is something we are working towards. We are currently looking for members who can drive so that we can organise car sharing. Members who are able to shuttle people in their cars will obviously be compensated for their petrol usage.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: I don’t drive, but I’d be happy to contribute some money in order to use the shuttle services.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: Yes. That is no problem. Are you aware of when the meetings take place?
Speaker 2: Potential Member: No. I couldn’t find the meeting times on your website.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: We hold meetings from 6 to 8PM every Tuesday.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Ah, that’s lucky. I go to a debating club every Wednesday, so I’m glad that it’s on a different night so I can attend both. Do you operate year round?
Speaker 1: Society Representative: We used to close during December for the Christmas period, but we found that a lot of members wanted to continue their practices during this time. We operate for most of the year, but we do, however, close for August because the weather gets so hot that we are unable to practice comfortably. This may change when we have enough funds to operate the air conditioning.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Okay. I also wanted to ask how much the membership fee is and what is included with it.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: Our membership fee is inexpensive, and it includes many benefits that certainly make the costs worth it. For example, we hold an annual event where members can meet each other and converse about topics that they have in common. We find that this is very popular, as the dinner is truly superb and included with your membership fee.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Wow, that sounds great! And how much does membership cost?
Speaker 1: Society Representative: We have a couple of membership rates depending on your age and situation. For employed members under the age of 30, the fee is £40, while it costs £60 for members aged between 30 and 60. Which of these categories do you fit into?
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Oh, I don’t fit into either of those. I’m 65 years old and retired, so I’m no longer employed.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: That’s no problem at all. You qualify for the lowest price membership fee of £25 which applies to those who are either unemployed or retired.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Wow, that’s really affordable. I was thinking of bringing my grandson along to some of the practices, so what would the membership cost for him? He’s 14.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: I’m afraid that the club is for adults only. That is to say, we don’t allow members who are aged 16 and under. He is welcome to join in two years’ time, though.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Ah, that’s a shame. I guess I can wait and buy him a membership for his birthday present.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: Yes. What a good idea.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: I was hoping I could bring him with me so I have someone there to talk to. I’m worried that I won’t have anything in common with the other members.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: I’m sure you’ll fit in just fine. All our members are very friendly and interested in culture and music. Most of the people involved are modern authors looking for new experiences to write about in their books. You could read some of their books so you have something to discuss with them.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: That’s a good suggestion. I’ll definitely do that. I’m really looking forward to attending the annual dinner, so I can meet new people and hopefully make some friends.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: Absolutely. Everyone has a great night, and it’s all for charity, as all of the money raised from this event is donated to the Children’s Hospital so they can buy toys and clothes.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Wow. What a great cause. Well, I will definitely be popping in soon to arrange my membership. Thank you for all of your help.
Speaker 1: Society Representative: No problem at all. Goodbye.
Speaker 2: Potential Member: Bye.
